wiki_text: The Suape regasification terminal (Regas), operated by OnCorp with Shell as an anchor user, is Brazil's first planned multi-user LNG terminal. Construction on the Cais de Multiplos Usos (CMU) berth began December 2022 under a temporary 4-year port-use contract (later extended to a 25-year concession). The project stalled for roughly two years because an unmapped sulfuric-acid pipeline from the Abreu e Lima refinery (Rnest) crossed the terminal site; a coexistence agreement between Rnest and OnCorp was reached only in March 2025. Antaq (Brazil's port regulator) opened a formal inspection (FIPO 43/2025) into the delay and closed it 8 Jan 2026 without finding irregularities. OnCorp signed a vessel-charter agreement in May 2025 (charterer later named as Energos, Jan 2026) but the specific FSRU vessel remains contractually confidential. As of Jan 2026, OnCorp president Joao Mattos targeted an October 2027 start.

wiki_text: Eneva's Pecem 'gas-to-power' hub broke ground 9 June 2026: a R$6 billion, 1,147 MW pair of thermal plants (Jandaia II and III) built alongside a dedicated LNG receiving terminal and berth ('Pier Zero', ~R$430 million of the total spend), described in press coverage as being built concurrently with the power plants ('construindo a cozinha e a linha de fornecimento ao mesmo tempo'). This follows Eneva's April 2025 SPA to acquire Ceiba Energy's Jandaia power plant and the proposed Pecem FSRU project (Cade-approved end of May 2025), already noted in GEM's researcher notes for this unit.
